newsitem.title: USA: Thomas & Betts to acquire Augat in stock deal.
newsitem.headline: Thomas & Betts to acquire Augat in stock deal.

text.p: Thomas & Betts Corp. will acquire Augat Inc., another maker of connectors and parts for electrical and electronics products, in a stock deal worth about $550 million, the companies said Monday.
"We will be one of the five largest companies in the electronics connector industry," said T. Kevin Dunnigan, chairman and chief executive of Thomas & Betts.

"Our products and markets are complementary -- not duplicative -- and the combination will enable us to offer our customers a broader line of sophisticated electronics products in higher growth markets."

Under the definitive agreement, which has been approved by both companies' boards, Thomas & Betts will offer 0.68 share of its common stock for each Augat share in a tax-free pooling of interests. The exchange ratio is subject to changes in the average price of Thomas & Betts' stock over a certain period.

Above a $41.50 average price, Thomas & Betts will offer stock worth $28.22 for each Augat share. If the average price falls below $32 per share, Memphis, Tenn.-based Thomas & Betts has the right to cancel the transaction.
Augat's stock rose $4.375 to $25.25, while Thomas & Betts fell $1.875 to $37.875 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
The deal is expected to close before year's end, subject to approval by both companies' shareholders.
Thomas & Betts said it does not expect the acquisition to affect earnings in 1997 or only boost them slightly, and raise profits moderately after that.
The acquisition is Thomas & Betts' fifth this year as the company seeks growth through internal expansion and acquisition.

Thomas & Betts produces connectors and components for worldwide electrical and electronics markets. It reported earnings of $23.4 million, or 58 cents per share, on sales of $349.4 million for the same period.

Mansfield, Mass.-based Augat makes connector products, with broad applications in the communications, computer, automotive and industrial markets. It earned $7.6 million, or 38 cents per share, on sales of $150.4 million for the second quarter ended June 30.
